paras: The lynching of three men at Butlerville, Arkansas, took place on the night of Sunday, June 4, 1882, when a mob took three Black men from officers at Butlerville, in Lonoke County, and hanged them to a tree. The men, who were not named, were accused of assaulting a thirteen-year-old girl, Annie Bridges, although an earlier report had called the story untrue. A Little Rock dispatch of June 5 carried the news to papers across the country, many under headlines presenting the hanging as just punishment.

According to the Little Rock dispatch, on a Sunday about a week earlier, around May 28, Butlerville was excited by a report that Annie Bridges, aged thirteen, had been "outraged repeatedly" by three Black men who left her at eight o'clock that night and fled. A later report said the story was untrue and that the girl had told it "to escape punishment for being out so late." The shorter version of the wire said simply that "the story was denied."

A special dispatch from Des Arc to the Gazette then reported that the three men had been caught at Newport on Saturday night, June 3, and brought to Butlerville. There the girl identified them, and on Sunday night a mob took them from the officers holding them and hanged all three to a tree. Condensed versions said instead that the men were taken "from the jail" or "from the police." No account names the victims, any member of the mob, or the officers, and none gives the size of the crowd.
No report of an inquest, arrest, or official inquiry appears in the coverage, which ends with weekly digests in mid-June.

Nearly all coverage came from the single Little Rock dispatch of June 5, which ran in two forms: a full text that included both the retraction and the Gazette special, and a short version that placed the event at "Butterfield." The Yankton Press and Dakotaian printed the short version on June 5, and on June 6 the dispatch appeared in Memphis, Wheeling, Savannah, New York, Washington, St. Paul, Seattle, Los Angeles, San Antonio and elsewhere. Weeklies repeated it into mid-June, including the Helena Weekly Herald on June 8 and the Elk County Advocate in Pennsylvania on June 15.

Most headlines treated the accusation as proven and the hanging as deserved: "A Brutal Crime Avenged" in Savannah, "Righteous Retribution by a Mob" in St. Paul, "Served them Right" in Los Angeles, and "Three Negroes Pay the Penalty of the Crime" in the Wheeling Register. Others labeled the victims "Three Negro Ravishers," "A Trio of Negro Fiends" or "Three Scoundrels." By contrast, the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer ran the same text under the heading "A Doubtful Story," drawing attention to the report that the girl had made up the assault. Several papers that printed the retraction still headed the item as a just punishment, while the New-York Tribune and Savannah Morning News printed the Gazette special without it.

The dispatches disagree on whether the alleged assault happened: the Gazette special treated it as fact, while the same dispatch reported an earlier statement that the girl had invented it. The place name also varies, printed as Butterfield, Butterville, Butteville and Bullsville, but the fuller dispatches give Butlerville, Lonoke County, and name Newport only as the place of capture.

reader.title: Lynching of three men at Butlerville, Arkansas
bases: Three Black men accused of assaulting a girl were taken from officers at Butlerville by a mob and hanged to a tree [A2, A7, A12].

Every account says a mob took the three accused men from officers (or a jail) and hanged them, without trial, for an alleged assault on a girl [A2, A7, A9, A26]; a mob or 'crowd of men' implies three or more.

All versions are Little Rock dispatches of June 5 relaying one Des Arc special to the Gazette [A7, A13]; no local, later or independent report was found, and the dispatch itself notes an earlier report that the alleged assault was untrue [A7, A12].

accounts.label: Short Little Rock wire
accounts.gist: Butterfield (or Bullsville) had been excited over a report that Annie Bridges was outraged; 'the story was denied', but the three were later caught, identified and hanged by a mob.

accounts.label: Des Arc special to the Gazette (via Little Rock)
accounts.gist: The three were caught at Newport on Saturday night, taken to Butlerville and identified by the girl; on Sunday night a mob took them from the officers and hanged all three to a tree.

accounts.label: Retraction report (in the full dispatch)
accounts.gist: Before the Gazette special, a report said the assault story was untrue and that the girl told it to escape punishment for being out late.

framing.detail: Headlines such as 'A Brutal Crime Avenged', 'Righteous Retribution by a Mob', 'Served them Right' and 'Three Negroes Pay the Penalty of the Crime' presented the hanging as punishment for a crime taken as proven.
The Wheeling Intelligencer headed the same dispatch 'A Doubtful Story', foregrounding the report that the girl had invented the assault.
Brief digests (Portland, Wilmington, Ridgway) gave the bare facts as a minor telegram, stating the men 'had outraged' the girl.

conflicts.note: The fuller dispatches give Butlerville, Lonoke county; the others look like wire or typesetting variants. Newport is where the men were caught, not where they were hanged.
The Des Arc special, the closest source, says officers; the jail and police versions appear only in condensed briefs.
